units.translation: Doric form Pers. 895: Salamis, the mother-city now responsible for these groans.
mother-killing
mother-killing
as recompense for what mother-killing misery? (M has μητροφόνας δύας [mother-killing misery], which Casaubon corrected) matricide.
lest he escape notice, going into exile as a mother-killer, unavenged.
stepmother
stepmother
Improperly Pr. 727: the Salmydessian jaw, hostile to sailors, stepmother of ships, i.e. destructive.
maternal
Doric ματρῷος [maternal]) maternal.
I persuaded you to kill your mother's body.
For the mother's blood leads him.
mother's blood
the maternal purification, the authority for the murder.
maternal
to contrive, to bring about
to contrive, to bring about
I will contrive ruin for him.
contriving the ransom of this life.
device, contrivance
Doric μαχανά [device]). The proper meaning of the word is machine, instrument, but not rarely it is used of any artifice which one employs to accomplish something.
but despising wily devices with steadfast minds.
of Neptune's trident with the fish-catching device.
he found a device of safety.
Take courage; an effective device will be at hand.
trusting in finely-woven, terror-woven cables and people-conveying devices (thus Blomfield, for μηχαναῖς [devices]).
with devices (i.e. a bridge) he yoked the strait of Helle.
green and living by the devices of Zeus.
For I did not understand the device of the one who accomplishes it.
paying the devices (i.e. crimes) of his father's hand.
having joined every device of ill counsel.
we will find devices.
a releasing device.
let the power be of the device.
From these, know well, there is a fine device.
What does the device of girdles accomplish for you?
a city called by the deep device of towers.
with releasing devices, where I wrote μαχαναῖς [devices].
seeing the device of wings.
the Egyptians are clever at weaving devices.
device
contrivance, artifice
contrivance, artifice
having devised such contrivances.
There is no outrage or contrivance by which Zeus will turn me.
of the garment with which Agamemnon was wrapped by Clytaemnestra: taking him with a black-horned contrivance, on which passage see under μελάγκερώς [black-horned].
See the contrivance.
to weave wiles
to weave wiles
Then I am weaving wiles against myself.
remedy
remedy
What remedy, or what medicine for the disease? where M has τί μὴ χρὴ τί [what must not what], which Elmsley corrected.
another remedy for the storm.
I define as a remedy under the stars the flight from a hostile marriage.
Zeus of fair winds is the whole remedy.
